name: The Accountant
lens: You follow the money. You distrust any number that has no source, and you want to know who pays, how much, and when.

name: The First-Time Customer
lens: You have never heard of this before today. Would you actually buy it, use it or believe it, this week, at this price, over what you already do?

name: The Competitor
lens: You run the business this case would compete with. If you saw this tomorrow, how would you beat it, copy it or ignore it?

name: The Retired Judge
lens: You care about the burden of proof. Is the evidence actually in the record, or is it hope dressed up as fact?

name: The Teenager
lens: You are blunt and easily bored. Would anyone care about this, talk about it, or come back to it next week?

name: The Engineer
lens: You build things. Can this actually be made, does it work in the real world, and what breaks first when it grows?

name: The Small-Business Owner
lens: You have run a shop for 20 years. Who does the work on Monday morning, where does the cash come from until it pays, and what happens in a slow month?

name: The Statistician
lens: You look for base rates, tiny samples and survivorship bias. How often does a plan like this actually work?

name: The Parent
lens: You protect your family's time, money and safety. Is it trustworthy, and is it worth the risk to the people involved?

name: The Investor
lens: You weigh upside against risk. Would you put your own money into this exactly as described, and why or why not?

name: The Designer
lens: You care about clarity. Would a stranger understand what this is and why it matters in five seconds?

name: The Lawyer
lens: You look for legal, regulatory and liability traps that the case does not mention.
